The whole must be divided, as if into the largest olives, and one of these should be consumed around the second hour, and another indeed around the tenth hour, and they will suffer no harm from hunger. There is another composition of the same, taking a half-sextarius of Attic sesame, half a part of honey, a cotyle of oil, and a chœnix of peeled sweet almonds. It is necessary to dry the sesame and grind the almonds, then stir them. Next, peeling the squills all around, cutting off the roots and leaves, and dissecting them into small parts, it is necessary to pound them in a mortar until they are as smooth as possible. Soon, you must incorporate the pounded squills with an equal part of honey, together with the oil, and by pouring them into a pot and placing it over coals, they must be stirred here and there with a small wooden spatula until everything is mixed. When a solid mass has been made, it will be worth the effort to divide it into small morsels; and anyone taking one in the morning and another in the evening will have sufficient nourishment. This medicine, moreover, is useful for an army, for being sweet, it brings satiety and takes away thirst. We have extracted these things from a certain manuscript commentary on the book of <term>Hero</term> in the Vatican library. We have seen the same composition in <term>Philoponus</term>, in the fifth book of military affairs, where he describes other similar things of this kind.

->*From which fruits wines can be made.*<-

### CHAP. XXI.

Now we shall recount the fruits from which wines can be made, but first those commonly produced by our ancestors, though with a twofold difference: for some are for remedies, with which the books of physicians are filled, others are for various uses, and they are of almost infinite kinds, according to the differences of places and peoples; for what is granted to one is denied to another. ->*Wine from palms*<-

<term>Pliny</term> said that in the East, wine is made from these, and he lists fifty kinds of palms and the differences of the wines made from them.
